articles.title: Trump's Supreme Court majority faces looming threat after Dem Senate takeover: 'Stuck'
articles.summary: Justice Samuel Alito confirmed he has no plans to retire, but Democrats' Senate takeover raises stakes for the Supreme Court's conservative majority.
articles.body:
Republicans' loss of the U.S. Senate in the midterm elections could have far-reaching consequences for President Donald Trump's judicial agenda, threatening his ability to reshape the federal courts and raising new questions about the future of the Supreme Court's 6-3 conservative majority.

With Democrats set to take control of the Senate in January, Republicans face a shrinking window to confirm Trump's judicial nominees, while any future Supreme Court vacancy could leave the president dependent on Democratic support to install a replacement.

"Lawless Lawfare" author Alex Swoyer told Fox News Digital the election results could leave the court's oldest conservative justices with a difficult decision over when to retire.

"It's likely the justices — mainly Justices Thomas and Alito — are stuck on the high court for at least six more years with Democrats taking control," Swoyer said. "Both in their late 70s, I could see why they may want to retire now, midterm."

Justice Clarence Thomas, 78, and Justice Samuel Alito, 76, are the court's two oldest conservatives, making their retirement decisions particularly consequential as Republicans prepare to lose control of the Senate.

Alito, however, confirmed to Fox News on Thursday that he has no plans to retire and is committed to serving through at least the current Supreme Court term , with the justices expected to wrap up their major decisions in late June or early July.

"While Senate Republicans were able to confirm Justice Barrett in a one-month timeframe in 2020, I don't think this GOP Senate has that same work ethic or ability to push a nominee through ahead of January," Swoyer said.

"I think conservatives would like to see them try; however, a judicial nominations expert told me the Senate work calendar ahead of the holidays would not afford them enough time," she added. "While a five-week window seems workable, it doesn't appear like Senate Majority Leader John Thune would have the support to usher such a move at this time."

The stakes extend beyond the Supreme Court. As of Nov. 8, the federal judiciary had 28 vacancies, with 16 nominees awaiting confirmation for current and future vacancies, leaving Republicans with limited time to advance Trump's picks before Democrats take control of the Senate.

Zack Smith, a senior legal fellow for courts and the Constitution at the Heritage Foundation, said Republicans should focus on confirming Trump's remaining lower-court nominees before their majority expires.

"The top priority for Senate Republicans right now should be confirming the lower federal court judges President Trump has already nominated. It will take all senators showing up and doing their part. But it is possible," Smith told Fox News Digital.

"As for the Supreme Court, even if a justice announced his or her retirement today, it could prove difficult to get a replacement confirmed before the end of the current Senate, although Senate Republican leadership has indicated a willingness to try. However, neither Justice Alito nor Justice Thomas has indicated any plan to retire."

The uncertainty surrounding Thomas and Alito echoes the debate over the late liberal Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, who resisted calls to retire before the 2014 midterms despite concerns that Republicans could take control of the Senate and complicate efforts to confirm an Obama-appointed successor.

Republicans won the Senate in 2014 and, two years later, refused to consider Obama's Supreme Court nominee, Merrick Garland, following Justice Antonin Scalia's death. Trump won the 2016 election and appointed Neil Gorsuch to Scalia's seat in 2017.

Ginsburg remained on the bench until her death in September 2020, just weeks before the presidential election. Trump nominated Amy Coney Barrett to replace her, and the Republican-controlled Senate confirmed Barrett days before Election Day.

Barrett's confirmation gave conservatives a 6-3 majority on the Supreme Court, a balance that has shaped some of the nation's most consequential legal decisions, including the 2022 ruling overturning Roe v. Wade .

articles.title: Lula, Milei e líderes de mais de 20 países defendem que próximo secretário-geral da ONU seja latino | G1
articles.standfirst: Atual secretário-geral, Antônio Guterres encerrará mandato neste ano. Brasil apoiava candidatura de Michelle Bachelet para o cargo, mas ex-presidente do Chile retirou candidatura.
articles.summary: Atual secretário-geral, Antônio Guterres encerrará mandato neste ano. Brasil apoiava candidatura de Michelle Bachelet para o cargo, mas ex-presidente do Chile retirou candidatura.
articles.body:
Os presidentes Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), Javier Milei (Argentina), Miguel Díaz-Canel (Cuba) e Delcy Rodríguez (Venezuela), além de cerca de outros 20 líderes de países da Comunidade dos Estados Latino-Americanos e Caribenhos (Celac), enviaram uma carta ao Conselho de Segurança da Organização das Nações Unidas ( ONU ) na qual defenderam que o próximo secretário-geral da entidade seja um latino-americano.

O mandato do atual secretário-geral, o português António Guterres, se encerra neste ano. O sucessor será eleito para um mandato de 5 anos, e o Brasil vem defendendo que, além de latino, o próximo chefe da ONU seja uma mulher.

"Convencidos da importância de promover um sistema internacional mais inclusivo e representativo, ratificamos que chegou o momento de que uma pessoa nacional da América Latina e do Caribe assumir a responsabilidade de ocupar o cargo de secretário-geral das Nações Unidas, em coerência [...] com o fortalecimento da diversidade na condução da organização", diz um trecho da carta.

O documento foi divulgado pelo Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Uruguai, que comanda atualmente a Celac.

Inicialmente, o Brasil apoiou a candidatura da ex-presidente do Chile Michelle Bachelet , mas, em meio à disputa, Bachelet retirou a candidatura . Desde então, o Brasil não formalizou apoio a outro candidato.

No documento enviado à ONU, os presidentes e primeiros-ministros dos países da Celac dizem que, se uma pessoa latino-americana assumir a Secretaria-Geral da ONU, fortalecerá a capacidade da entidade de "enfrentar os desafios globais, promover a paz e a justiça", além de "consolidar o multilateralismo e o direito internacional".

"Reiteramos nosso chamado respeitoso ao Conselho de Segurança e à Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas para que esta posição regional seja respeitada no marco do processo de consultas e decisões relativas à designação do próximo secretário-geral da ONU", conclui a carta.

Uma das principais bandeiras defendidas pelo governo do presidente Lula em relação à ONU é a reforma do Conselho de Segurança .

O grupo é formado por 15 membros, dos quais 5 são permanentes (EUA, Reino Unido, China, França e Rússia) - os demais ocupam cadeiras de maneira temporária e rotativa .

Lula vem defendendo que, além dos atuais membros permanentes, o conselho também conte com países como o próprio Brasil, além da Alemanha, do Japão e da África do Sul.

O presidente brasileiro argumenta que, se for implementada uma mudança nesse sentido, o conselho terá mais representatividade em relação à geopolítica atual.

Lula também critica que parte dos atuais membros, como Estados Unidos e Rússia, estão envolvidos em guerra com outros países (como Irã e Ucrânia), enquanto cabe ao conselho justamente evitar conflitos entre países.

articles.title: Trava extra para gastos, mudanças no piso da saúde e corte em benefícios tributários: entenda ajuste fiscal aprovado pelo Senado | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti, impacto das medidas será de R$ 60 bilhões em 2027. Senadores devem concluir votação da proposta na próxima terça (17).
articles.summary: Segundo ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti, impacto das medidas será de R$ 60 bilhões em 2027. Senadores devem concluir votação da proposta na próxima terça (17).
articles.body:
O texto-base do projeto de ajuste fiscal aprovado pelo Senado Federal nesta quinta-feira (12) prevê mudanças nas contas públicas para tentar controlar a dívida pública a partir do próximo ano.

Com corte linear de 10% nos benefícios fiscais e mudanças no cálculo de pisos de gastos, o texto enfrentou resistência de senadores da oposição ( veja principais pontos abaixo ).

A proposta foi aprovada por 45 votos a 31. Os senadores ainda precisam analisar destaques a proposta, ou seja, possíveis alterações no texto. A expectativa é de votação na próxima terça-feira (17). Após a votação, o projeto segue para análise da Câmara dos Deputados .

O objetivo do governo é conter o crescimento das despesas públicas e aumentar a arrecadação para tentar estabilizar a dívida pública, preservando políticas sociais.

Um dos principais pontos do projeto é a alteração das regras de crescimento das despesas públicas. Atualmente, o arcabouço fiscal permite que os gastos federais cresçam, acima da inflação, entre 0,6% e 2,5% ao ano, dependendo do comportamento das receitas.

Com o projeto, em anos em que o governo precisar cortar gastos para cumprir a meta, o teto será de 2%.

O texto também amplia a possibilidade de corte de despesas , permitindo que o Executivo bloqueie recursos mesmo quando a projeção do resultado das contas públicas estiver dentro da margem inferior de tolerância da meta fiscal.

Ampliação do rol de gastos que podem ser contingenciados

Atualmente, somente as despesas discricionárias, aquelas que o governo pode decidir se e quanto vai gastar, podem ser congeladas temporariamente (contingenciadas, no jargão econômico) para cumprir as metas fiscais.

Com a proposta, os gastos obrigatórios que não estão na Constituição Federal também estarão sujeitos à contenção. Segundo o economista Felipe Salto, esse conjunto de despesas representou R$ 388 bilhões em 2026.

Neste caso e no do gatilho adicional para a contenção de gastos, as mudanças são permanentes e valerão para todos os anos.

O projeto prevê mudanças nas regras de concessão de incentivos e benefícios tributários. A principal delas é a efetivação de uma defesa antiga do governo: um novo corte linear de 10% em benefícios que o governo aos mais diferentes setores da economia.

O corte de benefícios é uma defesa do Ministério da Fazenda desde a gestão de Fernando Haddad (PT). No final de 2025, já houve o corte de 10%.

Outra medida autoriza o Executivo a limitar a utilização de créditos tributários para compensar impostos devidos à Receita Federal. Atualmente, empresas que possuem créditos tributários podem deixar de pagar certos impostos.

Pelo projeto, o governo poderá estabelecer restrições a essas compensações, com percentuais diferenciados conforme o valor ou o tipo de crédito utilizado. A medida poderá ser adotada em momentos nos quais o governo entre em contenção de gastos.

Na prática, a restrição pode aumentar a arrecadação em dinheiro no curto prazo, porque parte dos tributos que seria pago com créditos terá de ser efetivamente paga, com dinheiro, pelas empresas.

O trecho levou a duras críticas do setor produtivo. Em nota, 57 entidades criticaram o fato de o texto não determinar um prazo para as compensações retornarem depois de uma eventual decisão do governo.

"O texto não diz se o crédito retido será devolvido, em que prazo ou com que correção, e a regra valeria a partir da publicação da lei", diz a nota.

O projeto também prevê medidas relacionadas aos chamados supersalários do funcionalismo público. O texto estabelece um prazo de até 120 dias para que o Congresso aprove uma proposta que regulamente os pagamentos de servidores acima do teto – atualmente em R$ 46,3 mil.

O projeto não elimina diretamente os chamados penduricalhos, pagamentos adicionais que podem fazer a remuneração de servidores ultrapassar o teto. Isso terá que ser definido no Congresso Nacional.

O projeto altera a base de cálculo para determinadas despesas vinculadas à arrecadação, como o piso da saúde. O texto prevê que, até 2030, a receita do imposto sobre a exportação de petróleo não seja considerada no cálculo de determinadas obrigações de programação de despesas, como acontece hoje.

Segundo o ministro Bruno Moretti, a intenção é retirar receitas extraordinárias relacionadas ao petróleo da base de cálculo de despesas constitucionais. A exclusão dessas receitas reduz o montante que obrigatoriamente precisa ser destinado à área.

Moretti defendeu que a mudança segue a lógica de que a arrecadação com petróleo só cresceu de forma extraordinária devido ao aumento no preço do combustível causado pelo conflito no Oriente Médio e não é uma receita que é contínua, o que infla os gastos com o piso da saúde.

A ideia é não contar com ganhos extraordinários - que podem não acontecer no futuro – para a conta de gastos que são contínuos e devem sempre ser realizados.

A retirada dessas receitas do cálculo do piso já está em vigor em 2026, mas em caráter temporário. Com o projeto, a medida poderá ser prorrogada até 2030.

Uma medida para dar flexibilidade para o governo gerenciar o orçamento é a que muda as regras sobre recursos com destinos específicos, como os fundos públicos. Com o projeto, até 40% do dinheiro que não for utilizado dos fundos no ano anterior poderão ser destinados a despesas públicas previstas na Constituição.

Para isso, o projeto altera a Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal – que proíbe o uso dos saldos desses fundos. No entanto, o projeto atual mantém a proibição de remanejar recursos de áreas essenciais, como saúde, educação, segurança pública, seguridade social, desenvolvimento social e de repasses a estados e municípios.

Apesar das medidas de contenção de despesas, o projeto também prevê uma flexibilização das regras fiscais para permitir gastos com subsídios ao diesel.

A proposta autoriza o governo a desconsiderar até R$ 10,5 bilhões em despesas extraordinárias para estabilizar os preços do combustível na meta fiscal de 2026. Os recursos estão relacionados à concessão de subvenções econômicas a produtores e importadores de diesel.

Na justificativa do projeto, Jaques Wagner afirma que a medida é necessária diante dos efeitos da guerra no Oriente Médio sobre os preços dos combustíveis.

A exclusão das despesas da meta fiscal não significa que os gastos deixarão de existir ou de afetar as contas públicas. A medida apenas permite que sejam desconsiderados na avaliação do cumprimento da meta fiscal.

articles.title: Turnê da Xuxa em MG: Fã relembra promessa para ir a show em 1990 | G1
articles.standfirst: Rubiatriz de Almeida Correia tinha 11 anos quando pediu ajuda ao santo, em 1990, para realizar o sonho de assistir a Rainha dos Baixinhos na cidade do Triângulo Mineiro. Mais de 30 anos depois, ela ainda guarda a bandeirinha e a emoção daquele dia na memória.
articles.summary: Com a turnê da Xuxa em MG, a jornalista Rubiatriz recorda o esforço e a fé para realizar o sonho de infância em Uberlândia e a expectativa para o novo show da Rainha.
articles.body:
As lembranças de fãs de Xuxa sobre passagens da apresentadora por Minas Gerais ganharam destaque nas redes sociais após uma publicação feita pela cantora na quarta-feira (11). Ao anunciar a chegada da turnê 'O Último Voo da Nave' ao estado, a Rainha dos Baixinhos também relembrou apresentações anteriores em Minas Gerais, incluindo uma em Uberlândia , no Triângulo Mineiro, em 1990.

A publicação despertou a nostalgia de quem acompanhou a artista durante o auge do Xou da Xuxa. É o caso de Rubiatriz de Almeida Correia, que tinha 11 anos quando descobriu que talvez não conseguisse assistir ao show da apresentadora em Uberlândia.

A família estava sem dinheiro, mas a menina não queria desistir tão facilmente de conhecer a ídola. Moradora do bairro Presidente Roosevelt, perto da Igreja de São Judas Tadeu, ela decidiu recorrer à fé.

Em 28 de outubro de 1990, durante a tradicional procissão em homenagem ao santo, ela fez um pedido especial: assistir ao show da Rainha dos Baixinhos.

"Na procissão, eu tirei meu sapatinho e falei: 'Eu vou descalça para pedir para São Judas me ajudar a ir ao show da Xuxa e, se eu conseguir ir, vou balançar a bandeirinha no show'", disse Rubiatriz.

Na época, a mãe das meninas ficou sensibilizada com o desejo das filhas de assistir à apresentação. Depois da missa, veio a notícia que transformaria aquele dia em uma lembrança inesquecível.

"Não sei o que aconteceu que, do nada, minha mãe decidiu nos levar. Eu quase morri de alegria. Depois da missa, ela disse que iria levar", relembrou.

Xuxa relembra passagem por MG em postagem — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Bandeirinha balançando e emoção por a Xuxa

A passagem da artista por Uberlândia provocou grande comoção. Imagens da época mostram ruas tomadas por fãs, entre crianças e adultos que tentavam chegar perto da apresentadora, entregar cartinhas e demonstrar carinho.

No dia do espetáculo, Rubiatriz e a mãe ficaram no meio da multidão. Mas a pequena fã não conseguia enxergar direito o palco.

"Eu era muito pequena, minha mãe era baixinha e eu não conseguia ver o show, só escutava. Minha mãe me pegava no colo para eu ver um pouco. Tinham uns rapazes que perguntaram se queriam que me colocassem no ombro para ver a apresentação", lembrou.

"Quando minha mãe deixou um deles me colocar nos ombros, eu comecei a pagar minha promessa e fiquei até o fim do show balançando a bandeirinha", contou.

Show da Xuxa na cidade — Foto: Reprodução/TV Integração

A lembrança daquele período também envolve a transição entre os programas infantis da televisão. Rubiatriz conta que acompanhou os últimos momentos do Balão Mágico e aguardava a estreia do programa de Xuxa. A identificação com a apresentadora foi imediata.

"Eu fui fã desde o primeiro dia. Acho que eram duas coisas que chamavam minha atenção: a beleza dela, por parecer uma boneca, e a simpatia", explicou.

Durante a apresentação em Uberlândia, Xuxa fez questão de demonstrar o carinho pelos mineiros:

"Eu não adoro vocês, eu amo vocês. Eu adoro vir a Minas Gerais, qualquer parte de Minas. Falou com o sotaque mineiro já dá vontade de abraçar, deixar minha marquinha", afirmou a apresentadora.

Aos 47 anos, Rubiariz trabalha como DJ — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A menina que fez a promessa para conseguir assistir ao show cresceu, mas o carinho pela Rainha dos Baixinhos continua. Hoje, aos 47 anos, Rubiatriz é jornalista por formação, influenciadora digital e DJ.

Ela conta que já não acompanha a carreira da artista com a mesma intensidade de quando era criança, mas ainda imagina como seria reencontrá-la. As duas chegaram a se conhecer durante gravações do Planeta Xuxa.

Durante as gravações, Rubiatriz chegou a ficar no palco e guarda uma lembrança curiosa dos bastidores: nos intervalos do programa, Xuxa saía para amamentar a filha.

"Já se passou muito tempo, claro que eu ainda admiro muito ela. Se eu encontrá-la novamente, acho que nem sei o que faço. Acho que pulo em cima dela e dou um abraço. Às vezes, ainda sonho que sou amiga da Xuxa", revelou.

O show é dividido em seis atos e reúne 37 músicas em 32 números, incluindo medleys. No repertório, estão sucessos que atravessaram gerações, como Doce Mel, Ilariê, Abecedário da Xuxa e Lua de Cristal.

Com cenários tecnológicos, projeções, efeitos visuais e participações de Paquitas de diferentes gerações, a apresentação passeia por momentos marcantes da carreira da artista, desde o Xou da Xuxa até Xuxa Park, Planeta Xuxa e Xuxa Só Para Baixinhos.

Nas redes sociais, em 2026, a apresentadora também demonstrou a ansiedade para reencontrar os fãs mineiros.

"Joelho tá desgastado (coisa de véia) e a coluna também, mas... O coração a mil, cheio de vontade de receber de novo o carinho de vocês! Amo chegar em MG. Obrigada por tantos anos de carinho e respeito", escreveu.

articles.title: Meta bate recorde e recebe meio bilhão de reais nas eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Valor pago pelas campanhas chegou a R$ 522,7 milhões, segundo levantamento com dados do TSE. A Meta recebe principalmente para impulsionar publicações de candidatos.
articles.summary: Valor pago pelas campanhas chegou a R$ 522,7 milhões, segundo levantamento com dados do TSE. A Meta recebe principalmente para impulsionar publicações de candidatos.
articles.body:
A Meta , dona do Facebook e do Instagram, recebeu ao menos R$ 522,7 milhões das campanhas eleitorais de 2026, segundo levantamento do g1 com dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

O valor é recorde, quatro vezes o de 2022, e faz da Meta a empresa que mais recebeu dinheiro dos candidatos. O número ainda deve subir: as campanhas do 2º turno, como as de Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), têm até sábado (14) para entregar a prestação de contas final.

Gastos com a Meta nas campanhas eleitorais. — Foto: g1

A principal fonte é o impulsionamento de conteúdo : candidatos e partidos pagam para que suas publicações cheguem a mais pessoas no Facebook e no Instagram e podem escolher o público que querem atingir. A Meta não produz a propaganda, apenas amplia seu alcance.

O impulsionamento é autorizado pela Justiça Eleitoral, mas não pode ser usado para atacar adversários. Clique aqui para saber mais . Os anúncios ficam disponíveis para consulta na Biblioteca de Anúncios da Meta.

O PL foi o partido que mais pagou por serviços da gigante fundada por Mark Zuckerberg: R$ 119,3 milhões, quase o dobro dos gastos do PT, de R$ 64,7 milhões. Em seguida vêm PSD, União Brasil e Republicanos. PL e PT também são os partidos que recebem as maiores fatias do fundo eleitoral , dinheiro público dividido conforme critérios como o tamanho das bancadas no Congresso.

Entre os candidatos, Flávio Bolsonaro foi quem mais pagou à Meta: R$ 18,4 milhões, 16% de tudo o que sua campanha gastou. Lula vem em seguida, com R$ 13,5 milhões (14,4% do total). Completam a lista dos cinco maiores Raquel Lyra (PSD), reeleita governadora de Pernambuco; Fernando Haddad (PT), derrotado no 1º turno em São Paulo; e Aécio Neves (PSDB), que perdeu a disputa pelo Senado em Minas Gerais.

A Meta recebeu em 2026 quase 23 vezes o valor de 2018. Sua fatia no total gasto pelos candidatos cresceu a cada eleição:

2018 (eleições gerais): 0,7% de todo o gasto dos candidatos.

2026 (eleições geral): 8% até o momento, segundo a parcial disponível no TSE.

Na lista de fornecedores das campanhas, a Meta recebeu mais de três vezes o valor da segunda colocada, a dLocal (R$ 141,1 milhões), empresa que processa e intermedeia pagamentos.

Na última terça-feira (10), o TSE multou a Meta em R$ 7,5 milhões . Por unanimidade, o tribunal concluiu que a empresa descumpriu ordens para garantir igualdade na distribuição e no alcance dos conteúdos impulsionados pelas campanhas dos candidatos à Presidência.

Durante a sessão, a ministra Estela Aranha defendeu regras mais transparentes para o uso de recursos públicos nos pagamentos à Meta. "Estamos falando de uma empresa que recebe 10% da totalidade do fundo eleitoral e temos praticamente nenhuma ferramenta de fiscalização de recursos públicos destinados a campanhas eleitorais."

O TSE ainda analisa outras ações, que podem definir se a conduta da Meta desequilibrou a disputa e se foi deliberada.

A Meta nega ter interferido na eleição. A empresa afirmou que cumpriu todas as ordens do TSE, que os problemas foram falhas técnicas corrigidas e que as diferenças de alcance refletem as estratégias digitais de cada campanha e a forma como as visualizações repetidas de vídeos são contadas.

Após vencer o segundo turno, em 25 de outubro, Lula disse ter enfrentado uma "intromissão das plataformas digitais" e defendeu a regulação do setor: "Não é possível que a gente não tenha consciência que o crime do mundo digital tenha que ser tratado igual ao crime da vida real".

Em pronunciamento na TV, no último domingo (8), o presidente voltou a criticar as big techs e afirmou: "A exemplo do que vem acontecendo em alguns países pelo mundo afora, as chamadas big techs tentaram interferir no processo eleitoral brasileiro, dando milhões de visualizações a conteúdos com desinformação e fake news."

Os dados foram obtidos a partir de arquivos de despesas contratadas da prestação de contas de candidatos, no Portal de Dados Abertos do TSE, gerados em 11 de novembro de 2026.

O levantamento também cruzou dados do DivulgaCand, plataforma do TSE, consultados na mesma data.

Para o cálculo das despesas, foram considerados apenas os pagamentos cujo fornecedor direto é o CNPJ 13.347.016/0001-17 (Facebook Serviços Online do Brasil Ltda).

Os valores estão em reais da época de cada eleição, sem correção pela inflação.

Foram excluídos anúncios pagos por apoiadores e pagamentos feitos por meio de agências de publicidade ou marketing digital.

articles.title: Trump on Colom’s Mississippi Senate win: ‘I give him a lot of credit’
articles.summary: President Trump reacted Thursday to Sen.-elect Scott Colom’s (D) upset victory in the Mississippi Senate race, giving credit to the Democrat for his efforts to win over Republican voters. “I don’t know the gentleman, but I give him credit,” Trump told sports commentator Stephen A. Smith in an interview at the White House. “I had…
articles.body:
President Trump reacted Thursday to Sen.-elect Scott Colom’s (D) upset victory in the Mississippi Senate race, giving credit to the Democrat for his efforts to win over Republican voters.

“I don’t know the gentleman, but I give him credit,” Trump told sports commentator Stephen A. Smith in an interview at the White House. “I had a rally there, and we had lines that went 10 miles long, and he campaigned on that line — telling everybody in the line what a good job he did. I give him a lot of credit for that.”

Colom’s campaign released a now-viral video on social media of him at Trump’s rally in Corinth, Miss., just days ahead of Election Day, in which he approached voters waiting to get into the president’s event and asked them which issues mattered most to them.

In the clip, many supporters cited high prices as key issue impacting their choices at the polls, though some openly expressed opposition to Trump’s war in Iran and tariffs. As of Thursday night, the video had nearly 239,000 views on Facebook and around 555,000 on Instagram.

After more than a week of counting late-arriving and affidavit ballots, Colom pulled off what was previously unthinkable: winning as a Democrat in Mississippi, a state Trump won by 23 points in 2024. The Hill’s election results partner, Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), projected Wednesday Colom had defeated Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R) by a margin of around half a point.

The victory was a major upset for Colom, who had just a 9 percent chance of beating Hyde-Smith in DDHQ’s pre-election forecast.

While the victory is a shock to many political observers, there were some indications of a competitive race ahead of Election Day. In the final stretch of the campaign, Trump rallied primarily in historically Republican states and districts, including in the Magnolia State for Hyde-Smith.

The president continues to insist, including in Thursday’s interview with Smith, that Republicans lost because he was not on the ballot — though he told voters on many occasions to pretend he was .

Colom became the first Black senator ever elected by popular vote in Mississippi and only the third in the state’s history — the other two being legislature-appointees from the Reconstruction era. Black Mississippians make up more than one-third of the state’s population.

The senator-elect and incumbent have history together; Hyde-Smith blocked Colom from receiving a confirmation hearing in 2023 after then-President Biden nominated him to become a federal judge. Now, Colom has blocked Hyde-Smith from winning a second full term in the upper chamber.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Nvidia chief quits' and 'Six women say they too were preyed on by Brand'
articles.summary: The resignation of Jensen Huang following reports he had an affair with a suspected spy leads a number Friday's papers.
articles.body:
Nvidia features prominently on many of Friday's front pages. The Financial Times describes what it calls the "spectacular fall" of Jensen Huang, who it says was allowed to mould much of the White House's policy on artificial intelligence. One major shareholder in the firm tells the paper the fallout will be "painful".

The i Paper says there is now a succession battle under way at Nvidia, and that Huang's departure "could disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped to shape".

The Guardian describes Huang as someone who rose from "washing dishes at a restaurant to a billionaire rockstar of the artificial intelligence boom". It says the current crisis enveloping him, and the company he ran, is "a lesson in humility that investors were not expecting Huang to receive decades on" from his job in the kitchen.

The Times sets out the stories of six more women who have accused Russell Brand of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour. The comedian was jailed for more than 10 years on Monday for rape and sexual assault. The paper says his lawyers did not respond to the latest allegations.

The Sun claims that Brand is being assessed for a transfer from Wandsworth Prison to the high security jail at Wakefield, which houses many sex offenders.

The Daily Telegraph says the Labour Party grandee Lord Blunkett wants ministers to slash their own budgets to pay for the welfare reform which is expected to result from Alan Milburn's review of youth unemployment. Writing in the paper, the former home secretary urges his colleagues to provide the government with "sufficient resource to kickstart this important work".

The Daily Mail says "eagle-eyed observers" have spotted similarities between Prince George's drawing of a kingfisher - which features in this month's Country Life - and a YouTube tutorial uploaded in 2019. The paper has spoken to the artist, Matt Fussell, whose sketch is of the same bird, from the same angle, in the same colours. He says: "While I can't say for certain whether he used my lesson, the similarities are exciting... and he should be incredibly proud".

images.caption: A number of Friday's papers splash on the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. It comes after the tech firm announced an investigation on Sunday following reports Huang had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Beijing has denied targeting the tech boss. The New York Times has also reported Huang had a second affair with an executive at the company. "Share price suffers as fears for succession grip investors", writes the Financial Times.

articles.title: Democrats can’t wait until after Trump to produce results, James Talarico says
articles.summary: DENVER — Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico told a gathering of Democrats Thursday that voters are expecting them to immediately deliver, and that means making President Donald Trump’s last two years in office the “most productive of any presidency in American history.”
articles.body: DENVER — Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico told a gathering of Democrats Thursday that voters are expecting them to immediately deliver, and that means making President Donald Trump’s last two years in office the “most productive of any presidency in American history.” Talarico, who just made history by becoming the first Democrat elected senator in Texas since 1988, urged his party to put aside vitriol and distractions and immediately provide economic relief to Americans. Democrats won both chambers of Congress, but Trump will remain in the White House — and wield the veto pen — until 2029. “The American people cannot wait two years for change. So we must work with President Trump,” Talarico said. “If President Trump wants the same plaques and portraits and busts as LBJ, we can help make that a reality.” It was a reference to President Lyndon B. Johnson, who was from Texas. Talarico spoke at the two-day What’s Next conference, an event organized by the group Majority Democrats, tapping into campaign themes he stressed on the trail. Then, Talarico said his goal wasn’t to turn all of Texas blue because he believes voters want a divided, but balanced, government. He also spoke against politicians who pit communities against one another, saying those in power wanted Americans to focus on the “wrong 1%,” instead of billionaires who were growing their wealth. In his speech, Talarico noted his historic win and what he described as a Democratic mandate “the size of Texas,” but stressed the need to reach across the aisle, and down Pennsylvania Avenue, to deliver results, even if it means Trump takes some of the credit. “We should make the final two years of his presidency the most productive of any presidency in American history, because this moment is so much bigger and so much more important than the red team or blue team,” Talarico said. “It’s so much bigger than a party. We are tired of being pitted against each other. We’re tired of being told to hate each other. It’s been 10 years of this kind of politics.” Whether Democrats deliver on an agenda and to what extent they focus on investigations of Republicans remains a central debate within the party. The White House has signaled it plans to fight attempts by Congress to investigate the administration. Talarico has previously called not only for accountability for the Trump administration, but also for Democrats to work with Trump. “It is not an either-or choice,” Talarico told NBC News earlier this month. “We need accountability and we need to deliver.” Talarico swept into office after campaigning against corruption and framing himself as David versus Elon Musk, the Goliath, who single-handedly spent more than $168 million to support Talarico’s Republican opponent, Ken Paxton. “We went up against the richest man in the world, and we won,” Talarico said at Thursday’s event.

articles.title: Boebert blames policy, corruption, ‘markets’ for possible loss
articles.summary: Incumbent Rep. Lauren Boebert (R) blamed her potential loss in Colorado’s 4th Congressional District on policy, corruption and “markets” Thursday as her race remains too close to call more than a week out from Election Day. “Yes, there are so many different variables, and I’m going to start with policy,” she told NewsNation’s Blake Burman.…
articles.body:
Incumbent Rep. Lauren Boebert (R) blamed her potential loss in Colorado’s 4th Congressional District on policy, corruption and “markets” Thursday as her race remains too close to call more than a week out from Election Day.

“Yes, there are so many different variables, and I’m going to start with policy,” she told NewsNation’s Blake Burman. “I’m a member of the House Freedom Caucus, and we were the ones that were having these floor debates when bad bills would come to the floor or deals that were promised weren’t followed through with.”

Although CNN called the race in Democrat Eileen Laubacher’s favor earlier this week, several major election results trackers, including Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) — a partner of The Hill, have yet to project a winner.

President Trump carried the district by 18 points in 2024, per DDHQ, but Boebert has struggled to pull ahead by a similar margin. As of 6:37 p.m. EST Tuesday, with over 95 percent of votes counted, DDHQ had Laubacher leading by 3,362, netting her 48.79 percent of the vote, while Boebert had 47.91 percent.

In her conversation with Burman, Boebert cited the congressional debate over Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) — which allowed the government to spy on foreigners located abroad — saying, “We were fighting on FISA to have warrants for surveilling American citizens.”

“We wanted fair elections, and there’s so much that we just weren’t heard on,” she continued. “We wanted to ban insider trading for members of Congress.”

Boebert said she believed this election, particularly, was “absolutely a cry that the American people do not want corruption from anyone, any time.”

The lawmaker added that “a lot that went wrong” throughout the election cycle, saying she and the American people “were played by the markets.”

When asked about what being “played by the markets” meant, Boebert said, “Everything is just dropping.”

“I have gas that is under $3 a gallon in my district now, when everything was closer to $6 a gallon just over a week ago,” she said. “And so there needs to be some accountability there. Also, we had legislation that would pause exports for diesel. We had legislation even to suspend the federal gas tax.”

“It’s not a lot, but it’s something to show that we do care about the American people’s wallets. “

The Democrat benefitted from a midterm environment that wiped out many long-term GOP lawmakers in both chambers. Boebert, a long-time Trump ally, attempted to distance herself from national Republicans by speaking out against the Iran war, but it is unclear if that will help her chances of staying in the House.

articles.title: Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer for majority leader
articles.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., announced Thursday he will run for Senate majority leader, becoming the first to challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., announced Thursday he will run for Senate majority leader, becoming the first to challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for the position. “In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies — but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen said in a statement. Van Hollen’s move follows attempts by grassroots progressives — and some newly elected Democratic senators — to draft him for the position as some seek an alternative to Schumer. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person — it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader,” he added. Schumer, who has led the Senate Democratic caucus since 2017, remains favored to retain the position of Democratic leader. Still, it’s likely to be the most serious challenge he has gotten for the job. Democratic senators will hold a vote in December to choose their leadership for the next Congress. That vote is held behind closed doors and requires a simple majority of the caucus. Van Hollen said in an interview with MS NOW Thursday night that more than 10 senators have pledged to support him. “We have a lot of people, but here’s the thing about an election like this: As you say, I’m the underdog,” Van Hollen said. “I told people I was thinking about it, and so now we are opening up the process, right?” He added, “Now people will have to make a decision, one way or the other, and they have to decide whether they want to vote for change or whether they want to vote for the status quo.” Van Hollen plans to run on having the new Democratic majority use every available tool to end the Iran war, starting with the upcoming government funding measure to avoid a December shutdown, according to his team. He’s also proposing to reverse President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill,” get money out of politics and tackle corruption. Van Hollen, 67, is newer to Congress than Schumer, 75, but both men have served in Congress for decades. Van Hollen was first elected to the Senate in 2016. Before that, he served in the House for over a decade, beginning in 2003. Schumer was first elected to the House in 1980 and moved up to the Senate in 1999. Schumer responded on X to Van Hollen’s announcement, saying he has the votes to win. “I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together—55 seats and counting is an amazing result—and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader,” he said. “I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people.” Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., said Wednesday that he would support Van Hollen if he decided to launch an official bid for the leadership role. The day prior, Sanders had said he would not back Schumer, saying at a press conference that “in my view, the time is now for change.” After Van Hollen’s announcement on Thursday night, Sanders wrote in a post on X that he would be supporting his bid to lead Senate Democrats. “The American people voted for change. They want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families,” he wrote. Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan endorsed Van Hollen for the role shortly after his announcement Thursday night, writing in a post on X, “I called on Sen. @ChrisVanHollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience.” “We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority,” El-Sayed wrote, adding that to “earn our mandate,” Democrats “will require bold leadership.” Still, Schumer has maintained support from longtime colleagues who point to his work as minority leader ahead of Democrats’ landslide midterm victories. “Chuck Schumer is one of the principal architects of the most successful election in modern history, and I see no reason to change the leadership that helped make that success possible,” Sen. Angus King, I-Maine, wrote in a statement on Thursday night. “Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?” King wrote that Schumer “outlined an aggressive plan for the new Democratic majority which is directly responsive to the message we heard from the voters, and he has the experience and unique mastery of the Senate process to make it happen.” Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., also urged Democrats not to turn their backs on Schumer earlier this week, saying that “no one has put in the time and effort that anyone has put into this cycle than he did.” Gillibrand, who oversaw Senate Democrats’ campaign arm for the midterms, said Schumer ensured that resources were provided to help 100,000 new voters register in Mississippi, where Sen.-elect Scott Colom just captured a stunning victory. “That takes vision. It takes clarity of thought. It takes strategic leadership, and that is what Sen. Schumer has done, and that’s why you will see, despite all the grumblings, enormous gratitude for the hard work he has done to get us to this position,” Gillibrand said.

articles.title: Van Hollen to challenge Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress, setting up a c...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer after the party swept to power in the midterm elections.

Van Hollen said in a statement that "the American people called for change" and that is why he is running.

"It's now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership," Van Hollen said. "This is not about any one person — it's about answering the call of the American people. That is why I'm running for Senate Majority Leader."

Schumer has said he has the necessary support to win the race, which will be the first contested election for Senaet Democratic leader in decades. The closed-door, secret-ballot election will be held in early December.

The question of whether to reelect Schumer has already divided the caucus and many senators have declined to say publicly how they will vote, even before Van Hollen entered the race. They have privately deliberated about what message to take from the election and many are torn — Schumer recruited many of the party's winning candidates and raised money for them, but progressive groups are pushing for his removal.

Making the pitch for his reelection, Schumer has been working with Democratic senators one-on-one to form an agenda for 2027. In private caucus meetings this week, Schumer opened discussion on a broad plan for their first 100 days in power that included health care and tariff legislation and efforts to stop the Iran war.

"I'm going to win it," Schumer told The Associated Press in an interview last week.

In a statement after Van Hollen's announcement, Schumer said he welcomes any discussion about the future of the caucus.

"I'm proud of what we've accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader," Schumer said. "I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people."

Divisions over Schumer have simmered over the last two years

While Schumer is the favorite to win, Van Hollen's run exposes a rift in the party that opened in the spring of 2025 , when Schumer was put on the defensive after he sided with Republicans on a spending vote.

Even as Schumer has redeemed himself within his caucus since then — leading them through a government shutdown last year and orchestrating huge wins in the election — many in the Democratic base are agitating for generational change.

Van Hollen, 67, is not that much younger than Schumer, 75. But he has positioned himself as a new face in the party. He has also said he is considering a run for president.

While most Democratic senators have either said they are supporting Schumer or are undecided, Van Hollen has at least two backers: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, who won a competitive election in his state last week, and progressive standard bearer Bernie Sanders .

El Sayed posted on X Thursday night that their majority will need "bold leadership."

"I called on Sen. @ChrisVanHollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience," El-Sayed wrote. "We need both right now. Which is why I'm proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority."

Sen. Sanders, an independent who caucuses with the Democrats, held a press conference Tuesday announcing he would not support Schumer. He posted Thursday night that the American people "want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families. That is why I am supporting Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats."

Van Hollen has not yet laid out his own agenda, but he has criticized Schumer for his ties to Israel and other special interests.

While Schumer has a long history of support for Israel, he has strongly criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his handling of the war in Gaza.

Several senators have said they are backing Schumer, including incoming Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown , who beat Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week. Beyond the election wins, those who support him say being the leader is a difficult job, experience is necessary and Schumer has proven himself with legislative successes when they held the Senate under President Joe Biden.

"Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?" posted Maine Sen. Angus King, another independent who caucuses with Democrats and votes in the leadership election.

"Chuck Schumer is one of the principal architects of the most successful election in modern history, and I see no reason to change the leadership that helped make that success possible," King wrote.

Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto, D-Nev., also posted her support Thursday evening:

Cortez Masto said Schumer was key in "securing a historic majority. I will be supporting him as our Democratic leader."

articles.title: Chris Van Hollen launches bid to lead Democrats in US Senate
articles.summary: Van Hollen’s leadership drive follows Democratic sweeps in elections and challenges veteran leader Schumer.
articles.body:
US Senator Chris Van Hollen has said he is running for Senate majority leader as Democrats gear up to take charge of the US Congress in January following a Democratic landslide in this month’s midterm elections.

Van Hollen said in a post on X late on Thursday that Americans had “called on us to unrig an economy rigged against working people & fueled by political corruption”.

“To deliver, we need new leadership,” he said, adding that “this isn’t about any one person – it’s about answering that call”.

Van Hollen has faced mounting calls to enter the race for Senate majority leader amid growing opposition to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer ‘s continued tenure after he faced criticism over his handling of the Democratic caucus during the Trump presidency.

articles.body:
Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) said he would challenge Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) for the role of majority leader on Thursday, setting up a showdown in the upper chamber as Democrats prepare to retake the majority.

In a post to the social platform X, Van Hollen called for “new leadership” in the Senate.

“In this election, Americans called on us to unrig an economy rigged against working people & fueled by political corruption,” he wrote. “To deliver, we need new leadership. This isn’t about any one person – it’s about answering that call.”

Schumer, who served as majority leader from 2021 to 2025, previously announced that he had the votes to return to the post, even as Democrats from both progressive and moderate sides of the party say they will not support him.

Sens. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.) appeared together at a news conference on Tuesday and said they would not back Schumer. Some incoming senators said the same , including Sens.-elect Adam Hamilton (D-Kan.), Annie Andrews (D-S.C.), Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) and Troy Jackson (D-Maine).

Sanders and El-Sayed both voiced their support for Van Hollen on Thursday night following his announcement.

“The American people voted for change. They want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families, Sanders wrote on social media . “That is why I am supporting Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats.”

Schumer appears to remain confident that he has the votes but said in a post to X on Thursday that he welcomes the challenge.

“I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together—55 seats and counting is an amazing result—and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader,” Schumer wrote.

The vote for Senate leader requires a majority of the caucus, and is a closed-door process that is scheduled for Jan. 4, after the new Congress is sworn in.

Part of the calls for Schumer to step down are due to his age, as he will be 76 years old by the time of the vote.

In an appearance on MS NOW Thursday evening, the Maryland Democrat outlined the differences between him and his opponent, pointing to his urgency to end the war in Iran rather than waiting until their party has the majority.

“I think that we heard loud and clear from the American people that they want to end the war in Iran and bring down prices,” Van Hollen told MS NOW’s Jen Psaki. “We should do it now. We shouldn’t say we’re going to wait till January.”

articles.title: Howard Lutnick agrees to testify as bipartisan pressure grows over Nvidia scandal
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who was also requested to testify, had previously praised the commerce secretary for his support and involvement in the industry.
articles.body: Facing bipartisan pressure, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed Thursday to testify before Congress over national security concerns regarding the expanding Nvidia scandal. The announcement comes after Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., chair of the Senate Banking Committee, sent letters Thursday to Lutnick and Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO earlier in the day after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. “Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions,” Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News. In the letters, Scott asked that Huang and Lutnick voluntarily appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively. Scott requested that Lutnick testify “for a public hearing regarding recent public reports about Nvidia and the Department of Commerce’s role that raises national security concerns.” “Given the Department of Commerce’s central role in issuing and enforcing export control regulations, your testimony before the Committee will be essential in our oversight of these efforts,” Scott wrote. Representatives for Huang did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Scott’s letter. Earlier Thursday, Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., told reporters that Lutnick should appear voluntarily, though if he doesn’t, “He may need to be subpoenaed.” Blumenthal said one thing he wants to know is, “Were export controls relaxed?” Sen. Jim Banks, R-Ind., said in an interview with Fox News that he’d like Lutnick to testify before Congress “ASAP,” noting concerns about chips being exported that should not have. “We have a lot of bipartisan questions and concerns about what’s happened over the last year that would allow some of these issues to continue, to chips being exported, it appears, to defy President Trump’s orders for those exports to be stopped,” Banks said. Huang’s extramarital activity has added to concerns that Nvidia chips may have been smuggled or illegally accessed by AI companies in China. Nvidia has said that it complies with U.S. laws on exports. Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., told reporters on Capitol Hill Thursday that Lutnick “certainly should” testify before Congress. “I think he should be given the opportunity and the strong encouragement to do it without a subpoena,” Cramer said. “If a subpoena becomes necessary, that would be too bad. But yes, he absolutely should.” Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said in a statement that Lutnick needs to “explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China’s military.” The White House has defended Lutnick, writing in a statement that the president “maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position as the most transformative Commerce Secretary in modern history.” Huang has previously praised Lutnick’s role in uplifting the U.S. efforts to lead in AI. “Howard is the person I talk to most in the administration — he’s on top of the technology and learning the industry quickly,” Huang said while appearing at a Nvidia panel alongside Lutnick in September 2025. Reps. Gregory Meeks of New York, Gabe Amo of Rhode Island and Sydney Kamlager-Dove of California — top Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee — signed a letter Monday demanding answers from Lutnick over the Trump administration’s “approval of advanced AI chip exports,” noting “concerning links to China” and “alarming reports of potential Chinese intelligence ties” to Huang. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., said Thursday that Huang had agreed to brief lawmakers, though the date and venue were still being negotiated. In a new letter to Huang on Thursday, Mast asked that he appear before the committee on Dec. 1 for a “closed-door, transcribed interview,” adding that a subpoena would be issued if Huang did not confirm the interview by Friday evening. Some members of Congress said they want answers from Lutnick much sooner than next month, when the Senate Banking Committee has scheduled its hearings. “Come here before Thanksgiving. Give us the facts,” Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said Thursday. Tillis, who is leaving Congress in January, said it would be wise for Lutnick to testify to Congress now, before Democrats take control of both chambers next year, adding the secretary “should recognize right now he’s got a lot of Republicans that are pulling for him.” “I’m not one of them, but he does,” Tillis said. “So it would seem to me that he would do himself a favor by getting in a room with Republicans, whether it’s a committee hearing or not, and lay out the facts so that he’s got a group of people that are generally going to take at face value what he says.”

articles.body: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., officially has a challenger for the mantle of Democratic leader, and incoming majority leader, in the Senate. Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who has become a progressive darling and outlet for those against Schumer’s bid for another term as top Democrat, officially announced that he was jumping in to challenge the longtime figurehead of the Senate Democratic Caucus. BERNIE SANDERS SAYS HE WON'T BACK SCHUMER AS PUSH FOR NEW LEADERSHIP GAINS STEAM "It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership," he continued. "This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader." Van Hollen, 67, has served in Congress for 23 years, first starting in the House before moving to the Senate in 2017. Schumer, 75, has been an elected official since 1981. The Maryland Democrat’s decision to run against Schumer comes after a listening tour with Senate Democrats, and follows his initial ambition of "kicking the tires" on jumping into the 2028 presidential conversation. REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: A USER’S MANUAL TO UPCOMING LEADERSHIP ELECTIONS IN THE HOUSE AND SENATE Since entering the Senate, Van Hollen has occupied Schumer’s left flank. It wasn’t until earlier this week that he fully took a shot at him, arguing that the longtime leader had chosen the "crypto industry," and the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) over progressive candidates that eventually won during this past midterm cycle. But he's managed to capture some of the superstars of the Left, most notably Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who pushed Van Hollen to run. "The American public spoke clearly last week. They rejected Trumpism. But we have yet to earn our mandate. That will require bold leadership. I called on Sen. [Chris Van Hollen] to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience. We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority." RACHEL MADDOW WELCOMES 'BIG FIGHT' BETWEEN SOCIALIST AND MODERATE DEMOCRATS AFTER MIDTERM WINS Schumer did not take the challenge lying down. "I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead," Schumer said on X. Schumer has maintained since Democrats flipped the Senate that he would be the one to lead them over the next two years. And one of his possible lieutenants, Sen. Our caucus has the right to have a conversation about the path ahead, but we have no time to waste," he continued. "We must move quickly to vote, unify, and get to work. articles.title: Dan Patrick concedes Texas ‘turned purple’ after Democrats’ historic blue wave
articles.summary: Outgoing Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick says the state has "turned purple" after Democrats swept statewide races but warns the GOP must fight back.
articles.body: Outgoing Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, a Republican, acknowledged Thursday that the Lone Star State "turned purple" after Democrats' so-called blue wave swept statewide races and flipped the governor’s office, a U.S. Senate seat and Texas House. During his latest episode of the "Lt. Dan Podcast," Patrick acknowledged that Texas’ political makeup is shifting left but stopped short of saying the state had turned blue after many others had described it as now a blue state. "Right now, I’d say it’s purple," he said. "We've been winning consistently, and people see it as a red state. But this time, the Democrats turned out more of their Democrat voters than Republicans turned out of their voters. But what really made the difference were the independent voters, the voters who don't vote in Republican or Democrat primaries. They only vote in general elections. "For almost every election, we’ve been winning those voters. We didn’t win them now. Will they stay voting for Democrats in the future? Two years ago, they almost all voted for the president. Four years ago, almost all voted for [Gov.] Greg Abbott, myself and the other Republicans. So, I wouldn’t say we are a blue state, but we’ve turned purple for this moment. TED CRUZ SAYS 'BLUE TSUNAMI' TOOK OVER TEXAS AFTER DEMOCRATS SWEPT STATEWIDE RACES "The wave election, a lot of factors involved from the top down, from Washington down to Texas and all the other states where Republicans lost," Patrick added. "I would say it's a group of voters who are willing to change their vote election to election depending on how they feel and how they feel about who's in charge. So, we're not a blue state, but we're going to have to work too hard to be sure in '28 and '30 and '32 we don't become one." Patrick, who ran for re-election but lost his race to Democrat Vikki Goodwin, was among the Republicans hit by Democrats' blue wave. Abbott, who was vying for a fourth term, lost in his re-election bid to Democrat Gina Hinojosa, and Texas Attorney General and U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton was defeated by Democrat James Talarico as part of huge Dem gains in the state and across the country, including in other traditional GOP strongholds. Democrats won every statewide race in Texas, bringing an end to decades of Republican control in contests that had once been considered sure bets for the GOP and leaving Sen. Ted Cruz as the only Republican holding statewide elected office. TRUMP'S GAMBLE ON KEN PAXTON BACKFIRES AS DEMOCRAT PULLS OFF HISTORIC TEXAS SENATE UPSET Patrick said Republicans lost voters in places and demographics they had gained in 2024, including the Rio Grande Valley and young voters. He joined President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance and other Republican leaders in attributing the party's disastrous showing last week primarily to voters’ frustrations over affordability and the Iran war, which has caused soaring fuel prices. Gas prices are about 83 cents per gallon higher than a year ago, according to AAA, which listed the national average at $3.91 per gallon on Thursday, compared with $3.08 a year earlier. "We were in a tidal wave, a tsunami that washed across the country where people just said, 'I can’t afford to feed my family. I can’t afford to pay my bills. I can’t even afford to fill up my car or truck,'" Patrick said. "It was almost to the point where, no matter what our message was, it didn’t matter. People were unhappy, and I get it." "People can agree with you on cultural issues or policy issues, but it doesn’t mean they’re gonna vote for you if they can’t afford groceries," he added. Patrick further acknowledged that the war in the Middle East has increased the cost of fuel but refused to denounce Trump's decision to attack Iran. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I totally support the president on that. If they had intelligence that Iran was gonna get a nuclear weapon, we could be in the middle of World War III if he didn’t take action, or Israel could have already been blown off the map," Patrick said. "So, I support what the president did, but the reality is that had an impact."

articles.title: Jones ousts House Democrat in California
articles.summary: Democrat Eric Jones will win the race for California’s 4th Congressional District, Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) projects, ousting incumbent Rep. Mike Thompson (D)...
articles.body:
Democrat Eric Jones will win the race for California's 4th Congressional District, Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) projects, ousting incumbent Rep. Mike Thompson (D) in a single-party battle.

The race had gone uncalled since Election Day, but Jones was projected the winner on Thursday, leading Thompson by more than 4 percentage points.

Thompson is the only House Democrat to lose in the general election this cycle. While Republicans flipped three Democrat-held seats — two because of mid-decade redistricting — all three were left open.

Jones ran a campaign focused on fighting corruption and lowering costs, highlighting his experience growing up poor but making it to Yale University on a scholarship.

A 35-year-old businessman without experience running for office, his defeat of the 75-year-old, 14-term incumbent is resemblant of fights for generational change in the Democratic Party.

California's top-two primary system allows the two candidates who receive the most votes to advance to the general election, regardless of party. The race in the 4th district is similar to matchups seen in Democratic primaries across the country this year.

In total, seven House Democrats lost renomination this cycle, including some to Democratic socialist challengers. Some of the incumbents who survived did so only narrowly.

The 4th Congressional District, based in the Napa-area in Northern California, was redrawn ahead of the midterms as part of a voter-backed effort to respond to Republican redistricting in Texas.

The district became less Democratic — though still solidly blue — loaning territory to the neighboring 1st Congressional District.

Democrats were able to get all five seats they attempted to flip through redistricting in the Golden State, including the 1st Congressional District, where Democrat Mike McGuire unseated GOP Rep. James Gallagher.

articles.title: Alito warns Congress can ‘turn off the lights’ at Supreme Court
articles.summary: Justice Samuel Alito, speaking to the Federalist Society on Thursday, warned against any potential congressional action to defund the Supreme Court as he defended the importance of an independent judiciary. “Congress can turn off the lights at the Supreme Court and stop everything from happening if they want to defund their activities. And there are…
articles.body:
Justice Samuel Alito, speaking to the Federalist Society on Thursday, warned against any potential congressional action to defund the Supreme Court as he defended the importance of an independent judiciary.

“Congress can turn off the lights at the Supreme Court and stop everything from happening if they want to defund their activities. And there are many, many, many other things that they can do, or at least try to do,” Alito said.

“So, it is important to preserve the independence of the judiciary,” he added. “If that is eliminated, then the Constitution as adopted in 1789 will no longer be the same.”

Alito made the comments in his return to the Federalist Society’s annual Antonin Scalia Memorial Dinner, named after the late conservative justice and held as part of the group’s annual convention each November.

This year, the convention comes a week after Democrats swept control of both houses of Congress. Alito made no reference to the midterm elections or the pending change in power during his remarks, but Democrats have eyed using Congress’s power of the purse as leverage against the conservative-majority high court before. Two of Alito’s colleagues — Justice Elena Kagan and Justice Amy Coney Barrett — made a rare visit to Capitol Hill over the summer to advocate for the judiciary’s budget and their increased security funding in the wake of rising threat levels.

Alito told the crowd of more than 1,000 conservative lawyers on Thursday that the judiciary is the least powerful branch and it is “vulnerable” to Congress and the executive. Still, the justice warned that judges can overstep.

“If you think about a hand grenade, a 500-pound bomb and a nuclear weapon,” he began, “the hand grenade is the last dangerous. But that is not to say that it is not dangerous.”

The justice chastised lower judges at one point for sometimes issuing “unjustified” orders blocking presidents’ policies in recent years.

“They are dedicated and they are skillful, but they’re not perfect and they make mistakes,” Alito said. “And in some instances, I think they have gone far astray in abuse of their powers.”

Alito was the latest conservative justice to address the Federalist Society’s annual dinner. Justices Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett shared the stage last year, and Justice Neil Gorsuch joined liberal Justice Stephen Breyer a year prior . Alito addressed the dinner virtually during the pandemic in a speech where he described the health crisis as having caused “previously unimaginable” restrictions on civil liberties.

The Federalist Society does not officially take political or legal positions, but the nonprofit over decades has become an incubator for Republican judicial nominees and a tentpole of the conservative legal movement.

articles.title: US Senator Chris Van Hollen seeks to lead Democrats: Who is he?
articles.summary: Van Hollen is known for his antiwar positions and championing progressive causes.
articles.body:
United States Senator Chris Van Hollen has declared that he is running for Senate majority leader as Democrats prepare to take charge of the US Congress in January, following a Democratic landslide in this month’s midterm elections.

Van Hollen said in a post on X late on Thursday that Americans had “called on us to unrig an economy rigged against working people & fueled by political corruption”.

“To deliver, we need new leadership,” he wrote, adding that “this isn’t about any one person – it’s about answering that call.

He is a Democratic senator from Maryland who has been in Congress since 2003, rising to prominence for his opposition during the second term of US President Donald Trump.

Van Hollen was born in 1959 in Karachi, Pakistan. His father was a Foreign Service officer who later served as the US deputy assistant secretary of state for Near Eastern and South Asian affairs.

His mother worked at the CIA and the US Department of State.

Why is he running for Senate majority leader?

Van Hollen has had mounting calls to enter the race for Senate majority leader amid growing opposition to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s continued tenure, over criticism of his handling of the Democratic caucus during the Trump presidency.

US Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed from Michigan has said he will not support Schumer as the majority leader in the Senate and welcomed Van Hollen’s decision to run.

In a post on X, El-Sayed said: “I called on Sen. Chris Van Hollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience.

“We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority,” El-Sayed said.

In April 2025, Van Hollen drew attention when he travelled to El Salvador to meet a Maryland resident mistakenly deported by the Trump administration, in a case which ultimately saw Kilmar Abrego Garcia returned to the US.

In September, Van Hollen forced a vote on a resolution that would have required the Trump administration to report on the killing of nine Americans in the occupied West Bank and on Israel’s treatment of Palestinian children in military detention. The resolution failed 47-53, with senators voting largely along party lines.

In August 2025, Van Hollen accompanied US Senator Jeff Merkley to the Rafah crossing at Egypt’s border with Gaza as Israel continued to prevent humanitarian aid delivery to Palestinians in the enclave.

Van Hollen has repeatedly challenged Washington’s relationship with Israel and has called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a “ chronic liar “. He told Al Jazeera earlier this year that the US-Israel war on Iran “is making America and our allies less safe”.

Van Hollen has been one of the foremost advocates for ending Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and violations in the occupied West Bank.

He has consistently pushed for strict accountability for Israeli actions and for restricting US military assistance to Israel.

articles.summary: El presidente del Gobierno estuvo presente en el programa de RTVE 'El Perro Andaluz'
articles.body: El último acto de precampaña, el plato fuerte empieza ya hoy hasta el próximo 29N, del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, fue en el espacio de RTVE 'El Perro andaluz' con Manu Sánchez y el dirigente político se explayó de muchos asuntos pero también fue al terreno de lo personal. Contó cómo se conocieron Begoña Gómez y él. "En el último acto de precampaña en Sevilla ha intervenido Begoña porque quería expresar el agradecimiento por el cariño que ha recibido de mucha gente. Nos conocimos en un bar, ella ya era profesional y llevaba muchos años trabajando en consultoría. Tuvo la mala suerte de enamorarse de un político sin saber lo que ocurriría, porque ahí solo era concejal. Ella es una mujer independiente, autónoma y me da pena que en este debate pretendan deshumanizarla", confesaba el presidente del PSOE. Ya en asuntos del día a día se centró mucho en lo ocurrido con el accidente de Urda, en Toledo. Manu Sánchez cuestionaba al presidente por la respuesta del Gobierno, las investigaciones, la seguridad ferroviaria y las responsabilidades políticas, incluida la dimisión de Óscar Puente como ministro de Transportes. “Durante esa semana hablé mucho con él (en alusión a Óscar Puente). Él me mandó un mensaje minutos antes de su decisión y era irrevocable. Me mandó un mensaje muy largo que no me deja margen", al tiempo que añadía: "Él tiene mucho criterio y toma las decisiones con mucho acierto. Y creo que fue el momento de hacerlo porque primero, aportó soluciones a las familias con el decreto ley, después aportando soluciones a la tragedia, rindiendo cuentas a todos con ruedas de prensa eternas y asumiendo la dimisión. Es extraño que se asuman estas decisiones, pero creo que ha dignificado la política”. De hecho, Sánchez seguía dando explicaciones sobre lo sucedido con el accidente y medidas a tomar. "Se ha multiplicado por 20 la inversión en la línea Madrid-Sevilla. Se hará una auditoría, pero lo que tenemos que resolver es si un sistema operativo, que no es que fallara, sino que falló el hardware. Tenemos que ver cómo podemos dar más capacidad al controlador y controladora para que el margen de error sea el mínimo posible, mejorar la formación de ellos, revisar las jornadas laborales con más descansos, simulacros de estas situaciones".
